title: Add idempotent migration plan replayer and timestamped snapshot lock for safer rollbacks
author: Avery Lin
release_notes: Adds a migration plan replayer to apply and rewind upgrade plans idempotently; introduces a timestamped snapshot lock and Helm/Terraform hooks to capture and export snapshot metadata for safe rollbacks.
commits: init: add migrate-replayer binary and plan v2 serialization
installer: add snapshot-lock controller and API
helm: pre-upgrade hook to capture snapshot metadata
terraform: export snapshot_lock_id and plan_checksum outputs
tests: restore/replay integration tests and teardown fixes
docs: upgrade playbook and runbook for replayer
description: Context: We have recurring incident post-upgrade where ad-hoc schema migrations combined with tenant-level state produced restore ambiguity. This PR provides two complementary features: (1) a migration plan replayer that serializes an upgrade plan and can idempotently apply/rewind steps for deterministic restore verification, and (2) a timestamped snapshot lock that binds a backup to a specific plan/commit so rollbacks can only use snapshots guaranteed compatible with the plan. || Motivation: Existing rollback paths assume backups are semantically compatible with target binary and schema versions. In private deployments this assumption breaks when operators run mixed upgrades or when incremental state changes occur after the snapshot. By recording a plan checksum and snapshot timestamp and exposing a lock ID we can (a) prevent accidental downgrade to incompatible snapshots, (b) run a dry-run replay against a candidate snapshot before committing a rollback, and (c) provide clear operational signals for SLA and incident playbooks. || What changed (high level): Added a new CLI 'migrate-replayer' under cmd/ which reads plan_v2 JSON, can execute steps idempotently, and supports a --rewind mode. Introduced installer snapshot_lock controller that issues a lock object with timestamp, plan_checksum, and snapshot_id and enforces TTL/rotation. Helm chart received pre-upgrade hook to trigger snapshot capture and annotate the lock ID into the release metadata. Terraform module exports snapshot_lock_id and plan_checksum as outputs for operators to reference during automated rollback pipelines. Integration tests simulate upgrade -> snapshot -> post-snapshot writes -> attempted rollback to verify safety checks block unsafe restores. || Backwards compatibility: Plan v2 includes a compatibility adapter for older plan_v1 files; the replayer will log when a migration step uses a legacy schema shim and emit a non-blocking warning. Existing installs that don't opt into the Helm hook are unaffected. || Checklist: - [x] plan format v2 defined and documented - [x] idempotency semantics implemented and unit-tested - [x] rewind path implemented with reversible steps where possible - [x] snapshot lock TTL and rotation policies implemented and configurable via installer values - [x] helm pre-upgrade hook and annotations added - [x] terraform outputs added for snapshot metadata - [x] e2e restore/replay tests added and passing after CI rerun - [x] upgrade playbook and runbook updated - [x] migration telemetry metrics and tracing spans added. || Commits summary: see commits field above for granular messages; notable internal changes: plan_v2 includes explicit 'reversible' flag per step, and the replayer adds a transaction journal to allow partial replay without corrupting DB state. The snapshot_lock controller exposes a ReclaimAfter annotation to avoid stale locks. || Files changed (high level): cmd/migrate-replayer (new CLI + unit tests), installer/controllers/* (snapshot lock controller + reconciler tests), api/v1alpha1/plan_v2.go (CRD-like structs used internally), charts/installer/templates/hooks/* (helm hook manifests), terraform/modules/installer/outputs.tf, tests/integration/restore_replay_test.go, docs/private/upgrade-playbook.md. No large model or binary artifacts added. || CI summary: First CI run surfaced a flaky e2e that failed in k8s-1.26 restore test due to timing assumptions in test harness; root cause was race in test teardown. That was fixed by adding explicit wait-for-snapshot-ready in tests and re-running CI. Linters initially flagged unused imports in controller tests; fixed in second commit. Final CI status: all checks passing. || Review conversation (abridged): Diego Morales: "Can the replayer operate in a streaming mode for very large plans?" Reply (Avery): "Yes, replayer supports streaming plan ingestion via stdin and a --stream flag; added a test for streaming large plans." Priya Singh: "What's the failure mode when a step is non-reversible?" Reply (Avery): "Non-reversible steps are marked with reversible=false in plan_v2; replayer will refuse automatic rewind and surface a manual rollback task in the runbook; test coverage included for refusal cases." Morgan Chen: "Ensure terraform outputs don't leak secrets." Reply (Avery): "terraform outputs only include snapshot metadata (id, checksum, timestamp); sensitive secrets remain guarded by existing KMS/HSM integrations; added an explicit note in docs." Reviewer approvals: Diego approved after minor nits, Priya approved after clarifying runbook steps, Morgan approved post CI green. || Post-merge operational notes: Operators should opt-in to the Helm pre-upgrade hook by setting values.snapshotCapture.enabled=true during upgrades if they want automated snapshot capture; otherwise use the CLI to create locks manually. The replayer CLI includes a 'dry-run' mode that performs validation without mutating data; recommended to run this against candidate snapshots before any rollback. The upgrade playbook now recommends keeping a retention window of 72 hours for snapshot locks to allow replay verification. || Rollout plan: merged to main, will be promoted to release/1.24.0 in the next maintenance window with a release note calling out new workflow for private customers and an opt-in flag for default behavior. || Risks and mitigations: risk of operator misconfiguration (mitigated by terraform outputs and validation), risk of overly strict TTLs causing inability to rollback (mitigated by configurable TTL and manual override workflow), risk of non-reversible steps (mitigated by explicit flags and runbook guidance). || Links: README snippet and upgrade playbook updated at docs/private/upgrade-playbook.md. Linear tickets: ENG-2491 (migration replayer) and ENG-2567 (snapshot lock lifecycle). Jira SUP-4127 documents a customer incident that motivated this work.
notes: Operators: prefer dry-run replay before any production rollback. See docs/private/upgrade-playbook.md for step-by-step commands.
